spots.summary: The Basilica Cathedral of Puebla, as the Cathedral of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception is known according to its Marian invocation, is the episcopal see of the Archdiocese of Puebla de los Ángeles (Mexico).

spots.name: Great Pyramid of Cholula

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Great Pyramid of Cholula, also known as Tlachihualtepetl, is a complex located in Cholula, Puebla, Mexico. It is the largest archaeological site of a pyramid (temple) in the world, as well as the largest pyramid by volume known to exist in the world today.

spots.name: Historic centre of Puebla
spots.summary: The historic centre of Puebla was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1987.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The International Museum of the Baroque is a museum of Baroque art designed by Japanese architect Toyo Ito located in Puebla, Mexico. It opened on February 4, 2016.

spots.name: Biblioteca Palafoxiana

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Biblioteca Palafoxiana is a library in Puebla City's historic centre, in the Mexican state of Puebla. Founded in 1646, it is recognized by the UNESCO for being the first and oldest public library in the Americas, It has more than 45,000 books and manuscripts, ranging from the 15th to the 20th century.

spots.name: Cuexcomate
spots.summary: Cuexcomate is an inactive geyser in Puebla city, Puebla state, Mexico. The sinter cone that the geyser built up around its vent is 13 metres (43 ft) tall and has a diameter of 23 metres (75 ft). A central crater within the cone is up to 8 metres (26 ft) wide and 17 metres (56 ft) deep.

spots.summary: The Chapel of the Rosario, located within the Templo de Santo Domingo in Puebla, Mexico, is an example of 17th-century New Spanish Baroque architecture. It has been called a candidate for eight wonder of the world.

spots.name: Cholula

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cholula was an important city of pre-Columbian Mesoamerica, dating back to at least the 2nd century BC, with settlement as a village going back at least some thousand years earlier. The site of Cholula is just west of the modern city of Puebla and served as a trading outpost.

spots.name: Museo Amparo

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: The Museo Amparo, located in the historic center of Puebla City, is one of the most important historical museums in Mexico. It was inaugurated in 1991 and sponsored by the Amparo Foundation, which was founded in 1979 by Manuel Espinoza Yglesias in honor of his wife.
